reasons: Tests were not run during this review.
Failure handling for adding all components is not tested.
The dry run test does not mock the command runner.

terms.meaning: a helper that prepares test data before each test runs
a fake stand-in for a real function so the test controls what it returns
a folder created for one test and removed afterward
a preview mode that does not change anything

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test file setup and imports
sections.what: Sets up imports and adds the scripts folder to the import path so the installer can be loaded.
sections.why: Likely reason: the test file sits in a subfolder, so the parent folder must be added for the import to work.

sections.name: TestShadcnInstaller (part 1)
sections.title: Test project fixture and setup checks
sections.what: Builds a temporary project with a setup file and component folder. Tests here check the default and custom folder choices, dry run, the setup file check, and that an empty project reports no components.
sections.why: Gives every other test the same starting project.

sections.name: TestShadcnInstaller: test_get_installed_components_with_files
sections.title: Tests for finding existing components
sections.what: Checks that component files are detected by name, that a project without setup reports none, that adding an empty list fails, that a missing setup file is reported, and that an already present component is refused.
sections.why: These tests protect the rule that existing components are not replaced by accident.
sections.watch_out: The success test expects the fallback version 2.3.0, so changing that version also requires changing this test.

sections.name: TestShadcnInstaller: test_add_components_with_overwrite
sections.title: Tests for overwrite, dry run and success
sections.what: Checks that the overwrite flag reaches the command, that dry run reports the command without running it, and that a successful add builds the expected npx command.
sections.why: Confirms the command is built correctly for each mode.
sections.watch_out: The dry run test does not mock the command runner, so a regression that runs the real command would download and run the tool.

sections.name: TestShadcnInstaller: test_add_components_subprocess_error
sections.title: Tests for command failures
sections.what: Checks that a failed command and a missing npx are reported as failures with a clear message.
sections.why: Confirms errors become readable messages instead of crashes.
sections.watch_out: Only adding named components has failure tests, so the failure path for adding all components could break unnoticed.

sections.name: TestShadcnInstaller: test_list_installed_no_config
sections.title: Test for listing without setup
sections.what: Checks that listing components in a project without a setup file reports failure with a not-initialized message.
sections.why: Confirms the list action handles the missing setup case.
sections.watch_out: Only the missing-setup case is covered by this test.

summary: Test file that checks the shadcn installer's behavior using temporary project folders and fake command results.
purpose: Confirms the installer handles missing setup, existing components, overwrite, dry run, errors and listing correctly.
why: Likely reason: the tests fake the command runner so they do not download anything or need Node.js.
how: Each test creates a temporary project with a setup file and component folder, calls one installer method, and checks the result text, the success flag or the command arguments.
inputs: Temporary folders created by the test fixture, and fake results or errors for the command runner.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest.
risks: Some tests depend on exact message wording, so changing a message breaks them. The dry run test does not block the real command runner, so a regression could run the real command.
debug: Run the test file with pytest and read the failing assertion. If a message check fails, compare the expected text with the installer's message. If a test runs npx, check the mock setup.
